extracted.intended_audience: applicants, agents and attorneys preparing or filing PCT international applications (international phase)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, filing and prosecuting an international (PCT) patent application during the international phase, including form/content/format rules, fees, searches and international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract must consist of summary of disclosure in description, claims and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.165-5.169. A figure of drawing may be published with the abstract (indication in request Box No. IX) (5.087, 5.170, 5.171). Characteristic chemical formulae should be included in abstract (5.165-5.168). Applicant may comment on any errors in abstract established by ISA (5.173).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments / new matter prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are not to go beyond disclosure in the international application (IA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 9.009, 10.070, 11.047. IPRP (Chapter II) will comment on amendments going beyond original disclosure (10.070, 11.047). Deadlines exist for taking amendments/arguments into account in IPE/IPRP (10.024, 10.028, 10.061, 10.068).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of disparaging and certain expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application (and statements accompanying Art.19 amendments) may not contain disparaging statements or certain prohibited expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and diagrams requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings (including flow sheets/flow charts and diagrams) are governed by specific presentation rules: arrangement of figures, margins, numbering, scale, when text matter is permissible, when photographs may be used, omission/rectification of sheets, color rules and when drawings are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.128-5.162, 5.129, 5.134-5.139, 5.130, 5.159, 5.133, 5.161, 5.131-5.133, 5.150-5.151. Rectification of obvious mistakes in drawings: 5.161, 11.038. Presentation/photographs/scale/text matter only if absolutely indispensable (5.131, 5.156, 5.159). Figure of drawing may be published with abstract (5.087, 5.170).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing format and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings (nucleotide/amino acid) must meet specific electronic format requirements and may be required to be submitted in acceptable electronic form with the IA or at later stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.099-5.104, 7.005-7.009, Annex C. RO/IB may require applicant to submit sequence listings with IA (5.099-5.100, 5.102). IPEA/ISA/DO may require sequence listings in acceptable electronic format (7.012, 10.063, 11.088). ISA is not required to search IA when sequence listings not in electronic form (7.013). Fees apply for sequence listings (5.101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand form content and election indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Demand form has specified boxes (I–VII) and contents; a demand must indicate at least one elected State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 10.012-10.034. Boxes: Box I Identification of IA (10.014-10.016); Box II Applicant(s) (10.017-10.018); Box III Agent or Common Representative/Address for Correspondence (10.019-10.023); Box IV Basis for IPE (10.024-10.028); Box V Election of States (10.029); Box VI Check List (10.030); Box VII Signature (10.031-10.032). Notes and fee calculation sheet annex guidance: 10.033-10.034.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing standards and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: IAs may be filed electronically with Receiving Offices prepared to accept electronic filings, subject to technical standards; electronic filing can give a fee reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.189, 5.188. Electronic filing must comply with Part 7 and Annex 7 of the Administrative Instructions. Fee reductions (including large reductions such as 90% in some contexts) may apply if IA filed in electronic form (see fee rules 5.188, 5.190).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements and order of the international application; minimum for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The IA must contain specified elements in an indicated order; a minimum set of elements is required to obtain an international filing date, and lack of required elements can affect the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.010-5.011, 6.005-6.006, 5.085, 11.034, 5.121-5.122. Number of sheets of each element should be indicated in the Check List (5.085). Lack of elements is a defect influencing the international filing date (6.025).

rubrics_metrics.name: International filing date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules define entitlement to an international filing date; the international filing date is not influenced by non-payment, incomplete payment or late payment of fees; certain defects do or do not influence the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.003, 5.007, 6.001(iv), 6.005-6.012, 6.009, 6.025, 6.032, 6.036, 6.026. Postponement of international filing date and related timing procedures (10.054). IA not published if no filing date accorded (9.012(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability as an IPE criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial applicability is defined for purposes of International Preliminary Examination (IPE) and is one of the criteria assessed during IPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 10.060, 10.001, 10.057. Lack of industrial applicability is a subject of comment in the written opinion and IPRP (Chapter II) (10.064(ii),(iii), 10.075).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: payment, allocation, reductions, refunds and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed fee rules: which fees are payable to IPEA or Receiving Office, allocation of payments, currencies, reductions (including reductions for electronic filing), additional fees for lack of unity, handling fees, refunds, due dates and consequences of non-payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 4.012, 5.184-5.199, 5.186, 5.187, 5.188-5.196, Annex C, 10.035-10.043, 8.029-8.036, Annex SISA, Annex E. Fee calculation sheets help identify fee errors (5.093, 10.034). Non-payment/partial payment consequences detailed (5.193-5.197, 8.032).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time limits rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time limits have specific allowances and prohibitions: extension not allowed for correction of Art.11 or Art.14(2) defects; extension allowed for Art.14(1) defects; no fee for extension for correction; extensions in force majeure situations provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 6.037, 6.053, 11.065D. See also general DELAY and TIME LIMIT rules (11.063-11.064).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence/documentary requirements for corrections or rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of right to file demand or IA, or documentary evidence, may be required to correct defects of residence/nationality or to excuse delay or loss; some documentary evidence is not required in international phase for certain rights (e.g., right to application on death of applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 10.046, 6.036, 11.063, 11.018B, 11.023, 11.089-11.093, 11.091-11.092. DO may require further documents for declarations under Rule 4.17(v) (5.075).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination / physical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: IA formal requirements (physical and formalities examination) are specified and must be complied with; formal examination may be applied to protests against payment of additional search fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.015-5.183, 5.184, 7.020, 11.066-11.071. See PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS and INTERNATIONAL BUREAU sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedures and consequences (including electronic/telefacsimile filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for where, when and how to file (including by telegraph, teleprinter, facsimile), definitions of filing and transmittal fees, consequences of non-payment, erroneous filing with non-competent RO and transfer to competent authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.001-5.199, 6.003-6.035, 11.067-11.070, 6.035 (erroneous filing with non-competent RO), 5.185 (transmittal fees), 6.059 (search copy only transmitted if fees fully paid).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Examination (IPE) availability and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: IPE is defined and available subject to conditions; IPE normally begins after the ISR is available; demand filing, fees, communication with IPEA, competence limits and access rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 3.003, 10.001-10.083, 10.004, 10.010, 10.051-10.055, 10.006-10.009, 10.013, 10.035-10.043. IPE report is the IPRP (Chapter II). IPEA may request priority document and translation (10.056).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPRP (Chapter II) content, access and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Report on Patentability (IPRP) (Chapter II) contains citations of relevant documents, comments on amendments beyond original disclosure, and statements on patentability criteria; copies/access are controlled and the IPRP (Ch II) is not binding on designated Offices (EOs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention / lack of unity consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity of invention (want of unity) has procedural and fee consequences (additional search/additional fees) and affects claims and treatment during IPE and national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.121-5.122, 7.016, 10.072, Annexes D,E. Additional fees may be payable for lack of unity; rectification and partial fees are covered (10.072, Annexes D,E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant right to comment on errors in documents/reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may comment on errors identified in ISA-established abstract errors or errors in translations of IPRP (Chapter II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 5.173 (abstract errors), 10.079 (translation errors). Fee calculation sheet use helps identify errors (10.034).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, confidentiality and access to international reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about international publication of the IA and ISR/IPRP, confidentiality procedures, timing of availability of copies (e.g., copies of IPRP made available after expiration of 30 months from priority date) and what is/not confidential during international phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 9.001, 9.012-9.029, 7.031, 9.016A, 11.073-11.074. IB publishes IA and ISR; confidentiality procedures apply for access to files and some copies only available after time limits (e.g., 30 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting of claims and description (form/content guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are specific guidance and requirements for drafting the claims and the description (including headings and how formulae should be presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Drafting of claims 5.112-5.113, drafting of description 5.094-5.099, headings for description (5.094), representation of chemical/mathematical formulae (5.107-5.108, 5.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of biological material and deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules apply when an IA contains a reference to biological material or its deposit, including identification of depository institution and possible procedures for obtaining samples in IPE/IPRP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Annex L, 11.082-11.085. Depositary institution for biological material (Annex L). Biological material sample may be obtained by IPEA (11.085).
